stem.en: In animals, in which method of fertilisation are the gametes more protected, and why?

text.en: External, as water surrounds and cushions the gametes

feedback.en: Open water carries gametes away and exposes them to other animals.

text.en: External, as many more gametes are released at a time

feedback.en: More gametes does not mean each one is more protected.

text.en: Internal, as they meet inside the female's body

feedback.en: Yes. Inside the body, they are away from currents and other animals.

text.en: Both, as the gametes of animals are always equally safe

feedback.en: The two methods differ. Gametes in open water are less protected.

explanation.en: In internal fertilisation, the gametes meet inside the body of the female. There they are protected from water currents and from animals that would eat them.

hints.en: Where do the gametes meet in each method?
